| Game type | Cards dealt per player | Max hearts a single player can hold |
|-----------|------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| Texas Hold’em (2‑card hand + 5 community cards) | 2 hole cards + 5 community cards (5 cards total) | **5 hearts** (if all 5 cards are hearts) |
| Seven‑card stud (or any 7‑card hand) | 7 cards | **7 hearts** (if all 7 cards are hearts) |

So in a typical Texas Hold’em hand, the absolute maximum a player can have is five hearts. In a 7‑card hand, it’s seven hearts. No special rule gives any player an advantage in terms of hearts – it’s purely random.

If you were thinking of a different scenario (e.g., a specific hand you’re analyzing, a tournament record, or a riddle), let me know and I can tailor the answer to that context!
